The Fed and global central banks remain in hawkish mode — the market is pricing approximately 33 basis points of additional rate hikes over the Fed's final two meetings of the year, with roughly 50/50 odds of a hike at the October 28 meeting, plus about 35 basis points of further increases expected in 2027. market_outlook: Adam's lean is cautiously bullish for Monday's session, driven entirely by diplomatic optimism around the UN General Assembly and hopes for de-escalation in the Middle East that could push oil prices lower. The key catalyst to watch is any signal from Trump-Iran or US-China meetings at the UN General Assembly — even a small positive development on the Iran/Houthi front could trigger an outsized oil sell-off with broad bullish knock-on effects across rates, margins, and consumer confidence.
bull_case: The single biggest macro tailwind would be any diplomatic progress at the UN General Assembly (September 22-28) that cools Middle East tensions — Trump signaled openness to meeting Iran's president, and China and Pakistan are reportedly urging Iran to rein in the Houthis. Nearly all of the market's current macro headwinds trace back to oil, so even a modest de-escalation could unleash a cascade of favorable effects: lower yields, reduced inflation, better corporate margins, and improved consumer confidence. The Trump/Xi summit on Thursday could also deliver modest tariff reductions and a trade truce extension, adding another incremental positive. Treasuries are catching a bid this morning, with yields down 2-3 basis points, supporting equity valuations.
bear_case: The weekend news flow was almost entirely negative — Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia escalated dramatically, Ukraine launched its largest drone strike on Russia hitting oil infrastructure, and a deluge of troubling AI headlines emerged including a delayed Anthropic IPO, underwhelming Anthropic revenue projections, massive OpenAI cash burn, and Oracle data center debt problems. Monetary policy globally remains aggressively hawkish with the BOJ, ECB, and Fed all hiking this month and more increases expected. Energy prices remain a structural headwind — motor oil is being rationed in the US, tanker costs are surging, and Qatar's energy minister flatly rejected Bessent's optimism about Hormuz becoming irrelevant, suggesting relief on the oil front may be wishful thinking.

Discovery, with Paramount potentially agreeing to preserve CNN's editorial independence and divest certain cable channels including Comedy Central. tts_summary:
Good morning. Here is your Monday September 21st morning briefing.

Markets are kicking off the week with a risk-on tone that frankly feels a bit disconnected from the weekend headlines. S&P futures are up about 49 points or 65 basis points, Nasdaq is up 110 basis points, and the Russell 2000 is up 47 basis points. Europe is broadly higher, up 85 to 120 basis points, with strength in industrials, basic resources, tech, and data center infrastructure names. Asia closed green across the board — Hang Seng up over 1 percent, Korea up 1.65 percent, Taiwan up 1.14 percent. Treasuries have a bid this morning with yields down 2 to 3 basis points across the curve. Oil is sliding — Brent down 170 basis points to around $102 a barrel. Bitcoin is surging 350 basis points to nearly $84,000.

So why are stocks up given a weekend full of bad news? The answer is the UN General Assembly, which kicks off Monday in New York and runs through the 28th. Trump signaled he would be open to meeting with Iran's president, who is expected to attend. He also reportedly called off air strikes against the Houthis at the last minute Sunday night. Markets are latching onto any hope that diplomatic progress could cool Middle East tensions. And here is why that matters so much: nearly every macro problem right now traces back to oil. If energy prices were to sustainably fall, you would get lower yields, reduced inflation, better corporate margins, improved consumer confidence — a whole cascade of positives. That is the bull case in a nutshell.

The bear case is straightforward. The weekend news was almost entirely negative. The Houthis dramatically escalated their attacks on Saudi Arabia, hitting a fuel depot at the Riyadh airport. Ukraine launched its largest drone strike of the war against Russia, taking out oil refining capacity. Motor oil is being rationed at US retailers. Tanker costs are surging. Qatar's energy minister called Bessent's optimism about the Strait of Hormuz becoming irrelevant — quote — completely wrong. And on the AI side, you had a wave of troubling headlines: the Anthropic IPO is delayed, their 2027 revenue projections disappointed, OpenAI is projecting roughly $280 billion in negative free cash flow between 2026 and 2030, and Oracle's Project Jupiter data center debt is struggling to find buyers. Fed speakers Schmid and Kashkari both reminded markets over the weekend that inflation is running hot well beyond just energy. The market is still pricing about 33 basis points of additional Fed hikes over the final two meetings of this year.

On individual names: Novo Nordisk is dropping in Europe after failing to give investors the specific financial targets they wanted at today's analyst meeting — a missed opportunity. Oracle faces pressure from the data center debt story. Paramount and Warner Bros. Discovery remain in limbo as California settlement talks on their merger drag on with other state attorneys general still opposed. On the positive side, Disney's parks business is holding up better than peers thanks to price promotions, and Amazon's logistics partner Kuehne and Nagel is rallying in Europe on a new long-term collaboration deal.

The week's key catalysts beyond today: flash PMIs Wednesday morning, the Trump and Xi summit Thursday, Meta Connect keynote Wednesday evening, and Costco reports Thursday night. The market is trading on hope today — diplomatic hope. Whether the UN General Assembly delivers anything real remains the central question. Stay disciplined and watch oil as your leading indicator.
